note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
The masters' book called us the most needy of any people in their country. It does say needy, and the Bible says it too: “The instruments also of the churl are evil: he deviseth wicked devices to destroy the poor with lying words, even when the needy speaketh right.”

The needy in that book is us. The churl devised wicked devices with lying words: cherry-picking “Servants, obey in all things your masters”, writing directions for masters to bring slaves to their religion, forbidding our meetings and our reading.

And even when we speak straight out of the Bible, going precept upon precept, they call it hate speech. That is the needy speaking right and the churl answering with lying words to destroy the poor. So when Colossians 3:22 is read in context, it speaks of Israelite servants and Israelite masters, and the lying words that turned it against us are the churl's devices.

precepts.text: A king shall reign in righteousness, and princes shall rule in judgment.
precepts.point: A king shall reign in righteousness and princes rule in judgment.

note.label: Political Power Under Darkness

precepts.why:
“But the saints of the most High shall take the kingdom, and possess the kingdom for ever, even for ever and ever.” The saints of the Most High, that is us. We are not going to ask anybody for the kingdom. We are not going to ask permission or say, can I have this. We are going to take it, and possess it for ever and ever.

Isaiah shows how we will rule it: “Behold, a king shall reign in righteousness, and princes shall rule in judgment.” The kingdom the saints take will be ruled in righteousness and judgment, not like the nations that rule us now, weakening nations and taking fields by violence.

That is the whole point of it: when the saints possess the kingdom, the king reigns in righteousness and his princes, the saints with him, rule in judgment, for ever.

precepts.text: Behold, a king shall reign in righteousness; that is what Saul was acknowledging, that David was operating in righteousness.
precepts.point: Saul made an acknowledgement there because he saw the righteousness of David: I know well that thou shalt surely be king, and that the kingdom of Israel shall be established in thine hand.

note.label: 1 Samuel 24: David Spares Saul in the Cave at Engedi

precepts.why:
“Behold, a king shall reign in righteousness, and princes shall rule in judgment.” That is what Saul was acknowledging: that David was operating in righteousness.

“Saul lifted up his voice, and wept. And he said to David, Thou art more righteous than I: for thou hast rewarded me good, whereas I have rewarded thee evil.” “For if a man find his enemy, will he let him go well away?”

Saul saw the righteousness of David, and so he said, “I know well that thou shalt surely be king, and that the kingdom of Israel shall be established in thine hand.”

precepts.text: Hear ye indeed but understand not; their eyes are shut lest they convert and be healed.
precepts.point: The eyes of them that see shall not be dim and the ears of them that hear shall hearken; you will begin to see spiritually and hear with understanding. The heart of the rash shall understand knowledge and the stammering tongue shall speak plainly.

note.label: Isaiah 32: A King Shall Reign in Righteousness

precepts.why:
“And the eyes of them that see shall not be dim, and the ears of them that hear shall hearken.” That is the undoing of what Isaiah was sent to say at the first: “Go, and tell this people, Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not. Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and convert, and be healed.”

Their eyes were shut and their ears made heavy lest they convert and be healed. Isaiah 32 is when that is lifted: you will begin to see spiritually and hear with understanding. “The heart also of the rash shall understand knowledge, and the tongue of the stammerers shall be ready to speak plainly.”

precepts.text: Christ quoted Isaiah: they could not believe because the Most High blinded their eyes and hardened their hearts.
precepts.point: The eyes of them that see shall not be dim and the ears of them that hear shall hearken; you will begin to see spiritually and hear with understanding. The heart of the rash shall understand knowledge and the stammering tongue shall speak plainly.

note.label: Isaiah 32: A King Shall Reign in Righteousness

precepts.why:
Christ quoted Isaiah on the eyes and ears. “But though he had done so many miracles before them, yet they believed not on him: That the saying of Esaias the prophet might be fulfilled”. “Therefore they could not believe, because that Esaias said again, He hath blinded their eyes, and hardened their heart; that they should not see with their eyes, nor understand with their heart, and be converted, and I should heal them.”

They could not believe, because the Most High blinded their eyes and hardened their hearts, just as Isaiah 6 said. So when Isaiah 32 says “the eyes of them that see shall not be dim, and the ears of them that hear shall hearken”, it is the turning of that blindness: you will begin to see spiritually and hear with understanding, and the heart that was hardened “shall understand knowledge”.

precepts.text: We forsook the fountain of wisdom; had we walked in his way we would have dwelt in peace forever.
precepts.point: When we apply righteousness we will be at peace among each other; this is the peace Christ and Paul preached among the brethren. Even our forefathers understood in captivity that walking in the way of God brings peace.

note.label: Isaiah 32: A King Shall Reign in Righteousness

precepts.why:
“And the work of righteousness shall be peace; and the effect of righteousness quietness and assurance for ever.” Even our forefathers understood this in captivity: “How happeneth it Israel, that thou art in thine enemies’ land, that thou art waxen old in a strange country, that thou art defiled with the dead, That thou art counted with them that go down into the grave? Thou hast forsaken the fountain of wisdom. For if thou hadst walked in the way of God, thou shouldest have dwelled in peace for ever.”

We forsook the fountain of wisdom; that is how we came to be in our enemies’ land, waxen old in a strange country. Had we walked in his way we would have dwelt in peace forever. That is the same peace Isaiah speaks of, the work of righteousness. When we apply righteousness we will be at peace among each other, the peace Christ and Paul preached among the brethren, and it lasts “Until the spirit be poured upon us from on high”, when judgment dwells in the wilderness and righteousness remains in the fruitful field.

note.label: Isaiah 32: A King Shall Reign in Righteousness

precepts.why:
“And my people shall dwell in a peaceable habitation, and in sure dwellings, and in quiet resting places”. We are not dwelling peaceably now; we are under the curse: “Cursed shalt thou be in the city, and cursed shalt thou be in the field.”

Cursed in the city and cursed in the field, because of the high crime and black-on-black violence among us. There are no sure dwellings and quiet resting places in that. So we wait on that peace to return, when hail comes down on the forest, the city is brought low, and the Most High’s people dwell in a peaceable habitation.
